rationale: Measured evidence on this exact revision (8c0ae97, clean baseline latency_ms 4.224596): the single forward runs 88 CUDA kernels whose active union is 4068.35us inside the 4.22ms synchronized window (kernel span 4145.1us, gaps only 76.79us), so the window is ~96% GPU-busy and launch-overhead-only fixes cap at ~1.8%. Kernel-time split (leaf, non-overlapping): conv2d 3035.6us (73.3%), batch_norm 427.1us (10.3%), relu 342.8us (8.3%), max_pool 199.3us (4.8%), add_ 121.1us (2.9%). The convs execute at ~19 TFLOP/s FP32 (~58 GFLOP / 3.04ms), i.e. at the Ampere FP32 roofline (scudnn/winograd kernels already chosen by heuristics) and TF32 is banned by the frozen numerical policy, so conv time has no legal headroom; the slack is the memory-bound pointwise chain. BatchNorm in eval is a pure per-channel affine (cudnn bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels, 427.1us) that folds exactly into conv weight/bias; the 8 residual add_+ReLU pairs (121.1us + same-size relu fraction of 342.8us) can run as one fused pointwise kernel per basic layer; the 76.8us of inter-kernel gaps can additionally be reclaimed by CUDA-graph capture of the static single-stream sequence. All of these edits lie inside one coherent editable boundary: the forward of ResNetForImageClassification (group eca3643289778aea5af3, target 'model', one call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa owning all 88 kernels and the whole module subtree). Replacing this whole bundle (rather than editing leaf conv/BN groups) is required so the inherited aten::batch_norm/add_/relu calls that the rewrite legitimately eliminates are explicitly excused by whole-bundle replacement instead of silently losing coverage; the replacement itself is invoked through the Python boundary on every run and must return the full [32,1000] logits computed on the current GPU-resident input.
hypothesis: Replacing ResNetForImageClassification.forward with a whole-bundle fused inference implementation reduces latency_ms from 4.224596 by roughly 12-16% (hypothesis ~3.55-3.75ms), tested by the framework's clean timing. The implementation: (1) at build time, fold every eval BatchNorm2d's affine (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta, running stats) into the preceding conv's weight and a new bias - mathematically identical, removing all 20 bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels (427.1us, 10.3% of kernel time); (2) keep conv2d/maxpool/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear calls numerically identical under the frozen FP32/no-TF32/cudnn.benchmark=False policy (convs are at the FP32 roofline and are not targeted); (3) fuse each residual add+ReLU into a single pointwise kernel (halves that tensor's memory round-trips, est. ~90-100us); (4) optionally, as a guarded second step, capture the static sequence into a CUDA graph during a legitimate first invocation inside the adapter's actual forward/inference_mode context (binding-contract compliant: replay on current inputs each invocation) to reclaim up to 76.8us of launch gaps. Quality risk is limited to FP32 rounding shifts (BN reorder ~1e-6..1e-5), expected to pass logits atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top1 and the negative control; measured acceptance, not prediction, decides. Convs, workload, batch, precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks are untouched.
